topic: NVIDIA Certified Professional AI Operations (NCP-AIO) certification exam preparation - administering and troubleshooting NVIDIA AI infrastructure with Base Command Manager, Slurm, Kubernetes, and Run:ai
exam_format: 30 multiple-choice questions PLUS 3 hands-on lab exercises in a single 120-minute online proctored session (lab environment is auto-provisioned at exam start; both sections share the clock). Pass/fail scoring. Professional level. Certification valid for two years; recertify by retaking the exam. Recommended prerequisite: 2-3 years of operational experience in a data center with NVIDIA hardware.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple select clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: MLOps engineers, DevOps engineers, solution architects, system architects, and AI infrastructure engineers who operate NVIDIA-based AI clusters. Comfortable at a Linux command line; the exam's hands-on labs run on live clusters with Slurm, Kubernetes, and Base Command Manager. Natural next step for students who passed NCA-AIIO.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Installation and Deployment
domains.notes: The largest domain, centered on Base Command Manager (BCM) and the Mission Control toolkit. Using BCM Base View to monitor cluster performance, resource utilization, and node health in real time; managing job scheduling and resource allocation through BCM's workload manager integration (Slurm or Kubernetes); applying patches, updating firmware, and synchronizing software images across cluster nodes; administering user accounts, roles, and permissions for secure cluster access; configuring and monitoring network settings for nodes, DPUs, and switches; diagnosing cluster issues (job failures, node outages, resource bottlenecks) with BCM; organizing compute nodes into categories by hardware or workload; documentation and usage/performance reporting from BCM. Installing and initializing Kubernetes on NVIDIA hosts with BCM; deploying DOCA Services on BlueField DPU Arm cores; installing Run:ai; installing Slurm.

domains.name: Administration
domains.notes: Administering Slurm clusters (partitions, QOS, accounting, node states, job priorities). Data center architecture for AI workloads: compute, InfiniBand and Ethernet fabrics, storage tiers, power and cooling considerations for GPU clusters. Administering Run:ai (projects, quotas, fractional GPUs, scheduling policies). Administering Kubernetes (GPU Operator, node pools, namespaces, device plugins). Configuring MIG (Multi-Instance GPU): profiles, partitioning A100/H100-class GPUs, MIG with Kubernetes and Slurm.

domains.name: Workload Management
domains.notes: Deploying inference workloads with Kubernetes (NIM microservices, Triton Inference Server patterns) and with Run:ai; deploying training workloads with Slurm (sbatch, srun, multi-node NCCL jobs) and with Run:ai; using system management tools (nvidia-smi, DCGM, dcgmi) to troubleshoot workload issues; allocating resources between teams with Run:ai, Slurm, and Kubernetes (quotas, partitions, priorities, fair-share); deploying containers from NGC (catalog, private registry, authentication, pulling optimized images).

domains.name: Troubleshooting and Optimization
domains.notes: Troubleshooting Docker (runtime, nvidia-container-toolkit, image and registry issues); troubleshooting the fabric manager service for NVLink and NVSwitch systems; troubleshooting Base Command Manager itself (node provisioning, image sync, daemon health); troubleshooting Magnum IO components (GPUDirect Storage, GPUDirect RDMA, NCCL communication errors); troubleshooting storage performance for AI workloads (throughput bottlenecks, filesystem choices, caching); troubleshooting NGC container deployment failures (pull errors, version/driver mismatches, entrypoint issues).

extra_guidance: Positioning: the professional-level follow-on to our NCA-AIIO course - reference that fundamentals (GPU architecture basics, AI workflow concepts) are assumed. Competing Udemy offerings are practice-test-only packs; this is a FULL video course with labs walkthroughs, which is the differentiator - marketing angle: 'the only full NCP-AIO video course with command-line walkthroughs, not just question dumps'. The four domain names and weights above are NVIDIA's official exam blueprint (Installation and Deployment 31%, Administration 23%, Workload Management 23%, Troubleshooting and Optimization 23%) - use them verbatim. CRITICAL exam-format point to hammer throughout: the 120 minutes covers BOTH 30 MCQs AND 3 hands-on labs on live clusters (Slurm, Kubernetes, BCM via Linux CLI) - every chapter must include concrete command-line sequences the student can practice (sinfo/squeue/scontrol/sacctmgr, kubectl with GPU Operator, cmsh/Base View flows, runai CLI, nvidia-smi mig, dcgmi diag), because lab fluency decides pass/fail as much as MCQ knowledge. Since this is a TTS narration course, read commands aloud sparingly - describe intent, show the command on the slide. Include a dedicated time-management strategy: recommended split of the 120 minutes between MCQs and labs. Cover classic traps: BCM vs Mission Control scope, fabric manager vs NVSwitch NVOS confusion, MIG profile naming (1g.10gb etc.), Run:ai fractions vs MIG partitioning, GPUDirect Storage vs plain NFS bottlenecks, NCCL_DEBUG usage, when a job failure is scheduler config vs driver mismatch vs fabric. Practice tests: 45 questions each, stay strictly on NVIDIA stack (no AWS/Azure/GCP service names), include Linux-CLI-output interpretation questions (given this nvidia-smi/dcgmi/sinfo output, what is wrong). Final chapter must be a full exam simulation walkthrough covering both the MCQ section and a mock lab-task runbook.
